subject: [RFC] Robust futex causing memcg OOM storm on exit

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the OOM victim still needs to charge memory to exit, but this can lead to contention on oom_lock and mmap_lock, causing a deadlock; suggested adding an early bail out in try_charge_memcg() if the current task is an OOM victim with mm_flags_test(current->signal->oom_mm) set
reviews.raw_body:
Do you mean, something like this?
--- 
diff --git a/mm/memcontrol.c b/mm/memcontrol.c
index 6dc4888a90f3..66f1eebf8c22 100644
--- a/mm/memcontrol.c
+++ b/mm/memcontrol.c
@@ -2648,6 +2648,18 @@ static int try_charge_memcg(struct mem_cgroup *memcg, gfp_t gfp_mask,
 	if (!gfpflags_allow_blocking(gfp_mask))
 		goto nomem;
 
+	/*
+	 * OOM victim still needs to charge memory to exit. OOM reaper should
+	 * help but it might fail on mmap_lock contention. If the victim is a
+	 * large thread group then all exiting threads might compete on oom_lock
+	 * just to learn that there is nothing really killable anymore. Bail
+	 * out early and fail the charge to expedite their exit. They are
+	 * considered fully reclaimed by the oom reaper and they shouldn't contribute
+	 * further charges.
+	 */
+	if (tsk_is_oom_victim(current) && mm_flags_test(current->signal->oom_mm))
+		goto nomem;
+
 	__memcg_memory_event(mem_over_limit, MEMCG_MAX, allow_spinning);
 	raised_max_event = true;
 

-- 
Michal Hocko
SUSE Labs

2026-07-28.patch_summary: The patch addresses a memory congestion control group (memcg) Out-Of-Memory (OOM) issue caused by robust futexes on exit, which leads to a storm of OOM events. The problem occurs when the kernel fails to properly clean up resources allocated for futexes during process exit. This patch attempts to resolve the issue by improving the handling of futex cleanup and resource deallocation.
